Diagnostic Communication Manager (DCM)

User GuideAI-GENERATED

Accepts diagnostic requests from testers, checks them, and responds to them with data from the fault memory and application.
AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: claude-opus-5-5 · Effort: high · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: c4fbaab8dd0b Provenance
Causal Anchor: R20-11 Valid from R20-11 Synthesized for this specification release.

Accepts diagnostic requests from testers, checks them, and responds to them with data from the fault memory and application.

The DCM is the diagnostic server of the ECU: it receives UDS and OBD requests via the PduR, checks them, and has them executed by the DSP or application callouts. A request is passed on only after complete reception [SWS_Dcm_00111]. Prior to this, the DSD checks service, session, security level, and mode conditions. If processing takes too long, the DCM adheres to the P2 time limits using NRC 0x78 [SWS_Dcm_00024]. It is only permitted to transmit in the communication modes enabled by ComM.

The DCM processes the diagnostic requests of external testers. It implements UDS services such as DiagnosticSessionControl, ReadDataByIdentifier, and RoutineControl [SWS_Dcm_00250] [SWS_Dcm_00253] [SWS_Dcm_00257] as well as OBD services [SWS_Dcm_00243]. Internally, the DSL manages communication and timings [SWS_Dcm_00027], the DSD checks and distributes requests [SWS_Dcm_00178], and the DSP executes the services. The DCM retrieves data from the DEM, from application callouts, and via RTE ports [SWS_Dcm_01263] [SWS_Dcm_00793].

Context diagram: The DCM between PduR, ComM, DEM, NvM, BswM, CSM/KeyM, and application SW-Cs. Sources: [SWS_Dcm_00094] [SWS_Dcm_01376] SWS DCM p. 209

After Dcm_Init [SWS_Dcm_00037], the default session and security level DCM_SEC_LEV_LOCKED are active [SWS_Dcm_00033] [SWS_Dcm_00034]. A request arrives via Dcm_StartOfReception, Dcm_CopyRxData, and Dcm_TpRxIndication. It reaches the DSD only after successful reception [SWS_Dcm_00111]. The DSD checks service identifier, session, security level, and mode conditions [SWS_Dcm_00196] [SWS_Dcm_00211] [SWS_Dcm_00217]. The response goes out via PduR_DcmTransmit and Dcm_CopyTxData [SWS_Dcm_00115] [SWS_Dcm_00092].

Sequence diagram: Reception, check, execution, and transmission of a request. Sources: [SWS_Dcm_00093] [SWS_Dcm_00351] [SWS_Dcm_00741]

Asynchronous application interfaces are called repeatedly via Dcm_OpStatusType [SWS_Dcm_00984] [SWS_Dcm_00530]. If processing takes longer than P2ServerMax, the DCM transmits NRC 0x78 [SWS_Dcm_00024]. Session switches via 0x10 take effect only upon transmission confirmation. S3Server timeout or Dcm_ResetToDefaultSession lead back to the default session [SWS_Dcm_00311] [SWS_Dcm_00140] [SWS_Dcm_00520]. The ComM modes control whether transmission is allowed. ROE and periodic transmissions run only in full communication [SWS_Dcm_00148] [SWS_Dcm_00123].

Errors usually become negative responses. If an application returns E_NOT_OK, its ErrorCode is sent as an NRC [SWS_Dcm_00678]. Dem errors are mapped to NRC 0x22 or 0x31 [SWS_Dcm_00704] [SWS_Dcm_00708]. After each transmission confirmation, the DCM releases the transmit buffer [SWS_Dcm_00352].

Role in the diagnostic stack: DSL, DSD, and DSP

The DCM responds to diagnostic requests from external testers. It implements UDS services such as DiagnosticSessionControl (0x10), ReadDataByIdentifier (0x22), and RoutineControl (0x31) [SWS_Dcm_00250] [SWS_Dcm_00253] [SWS_Dcm_00257] as well as OBD services such as $01 [SWS_Dcm_00243]. Internally, it consists of three submodules:

  • The DSL manages reception, transmission, and protocol timings according to ISO 14229-2 [SWS_Dcm_00027].
  • The DSD checks and distributes requests [SWS_Dcm_00178] [SWS_Dcm_00221].
  • The DSP executes the services and assembles the response data [SWS_Dcm_00039].

Downwards, the DCM provides callbacks for PduR (transport data) and ComM (communication modes). The diagram SWS DCM p. 209 still uses older names such as Dcm_RxIndication for this. Normative in R20-11 are the names Dcm_TpRxIndication and Dcm_ComM_NoComModeEntered [SWS_Dcm_00093] [SWS_Dcm_00356].

Further connections:

  • The DCM accesses the fault memory via the DEM API, for example with Dem_SelectDTC for ClearDiagnosticInformation [SWS_Dcm_01263].
  • It accesses application data and routines via configurable callouts and ports such as Xxx_ReadData or Xxx_Start [SWS_Dcm_00793] [SWS_Dcm_01203].
  • For diagnostic modes such as DcmDiagnosticSessionControl and DcmEcuReset, it is itself mode manager [SWS_Dcm_00775].

Context diagram: The DCM is located between PduR and the service providers DEM, NvM, BswM, CSM/KeyM, and application SW-Cs; ComM controls its readiness to transmit. Sources: [SWS_Dcm_00094] [SWS_Dcm_01376] [SWS_Dcm_00512] [SWS_Dcm_00868] [SWS_Dcm_01463] SWS DCM p. 209

Startup: Dcm_Init and the cyclic schedule

Dcm_Init [SWS_Dcm_00037] receives a pointer to Dcm_ConfigType with the post-build parameters [SWS_Dcm_00982]. From this, it initializes all global variables [SWS_Dcm_00334]. Afterward, the following initial state applies:

  • The security level is DCM_SEC_LEV_LOCKED [SWS_Dcm_00033].
  • The default session is active [SWS_Dcm_00034].
  • All ROE events are set to "ROE cleared" [SWS_Dcm_00872].
  • ActiveDiagnostic is set to DCM_COMM_ACTIVE [SWS_Dcm_01069].

Further startup tasks depend on the configuration:

  • Dcm_GetProgConditions detects a return from the bootloader [SWS_Dcm_00536].
  • With DcmDDDIDStorage = TRUE, DDDID definitions are restored from the NvM [SWS_Dcm_00867].
  • Failed attempt counters are read via Xxx_GetSecurityAttemptCounter [SWS_Dcm_01154].
  • When DcmVinRef is configured, the VIN is retrieved once with Dcm_GetVin [SWS_Dcm_01174].

Dcm_MainFunction [SWS_Dcm_00053] drives all asynchronous sequences. If an operation returns DCM_E_PENDING, it is triggered again, for example in the next MainFunction cycle [SWS_Dcm_00760]. The same applies to pending DEM calls [SWS_Dcm_01412]. Interpretation: The function is likely called cyclically by the BSW scheduler.

From request to response

Reception proceeds in three steps (SWS DCM p. 55):

  1. Dcm_StartOfReception reports the total length, the first frame, and the metadata [SWS_Dcm_00094]. If the request is too large, the DCM returns BUFREQ_E_OVFL [SWS_Dcm_00444]. For length 0, it returns BUFREQ_E_NOT_OK [SWS_Dcm_00642].
  2. Dcm_CopyRxData copies the segments into the DCM buffer [SWS_Dcm_00443].
  3. Only after Dcm_TpRxIndication with E_OK does the DSL forward the request to the DSD [SWS_Dcm_00111].

The DSD checks the request in several stages:

  • It searches for the service identifier in the active service table; if it is missing, a negative response follows [SWS_Dcm_00196] [SWS_Dcm_00197].
  • It checks session, security level, and mode conditions [SWS_Dcm_00211] [SWS_Dcm_00217] [SWS_Dcm_00773].
  • The overall sequence of checks follows ISO 14229-1 [SWS_Dcm_00827].
  • Configured manufacturer and supplier notifications (Xxx_Indication) can reject a request [SWS_Dcm_00218] [SWS_Dcm_00516] [SWS_Dcm_01341].

Activity diagram: The DSD allows a request through to the DSP only after passed checks; E_REQUEST_NOT_ACCEPTED suppresses any response. Interpretation: Order simplified. Sources: [SWS_Dcm_00197] [SWS_Dcm_00677] [SWS_Dcm_00678] [SWS_Dcm_00200] [SWS_Dcm_00827]

Transmission of the response proceeds as follows:

  1. The DSD requests the DSL to transmit [SWS_Dcm_00114].
  2. The DSL calls PduR_DcmTransmit with the configured Tx PDU [SWS_Dcm_00115].
  3. The PduR retrieves the data with Dcm_CopyTxData [SWS_Dcm_00092].
  4. Dcm_TpTxConfirmation completes the transmission [SWS_Dcm_00351].
  5. Confirmation goes to the DSP and subsequently to Xxx_Confirmation [SWS_Dcm_00235] [SWS_Dcm_00741].

Two special cases: If the suppressPosRspMsgIndicationBit is set, the positive response is omitted [SWS_Dcm_00200]. For generic connections, the DCM stores the source address from the metadata [SWS_Dcm_00848] and sets it as TARGET_ADDRESS_16 [SWS_Dcm_00849] upon transmission.

Sequence diagram: Reception, check, execution, and transmission of a request with TP callbacks and confirmations. Sources: [SWS_Dcm_00094] [SWS_Dcm_00556] [SWS_Dcm_00093] [SWS_Dcm_00092] [SWS_Dcm_00742] SWS DCM p. 479

Application interfaces, OpStatus, and response pending

Asynchronous interfaces take an Dcm_OpStatusType [SWS_Dcm_00984]:

  • The first call occurs with DCM_INITIAL [SWS_Dcm_00527].
  • After DCM_E_PENDING, another call follows with DCM_PENDING [SWS_Dcm_00530].
  • In case of cancellation, a call is made with DCM_CANCEL; its return values are ignored [SWS_Dcm_01413].
  • Output data and ErrorCode are valid only after the last call [SWS_Dcm_01187] [SWS_Dcm_01188].

Whether the synchronous or asynchronous variant applies is specified by the configuration (DcmDspDataUsePort). An example is Xxx_ReadData [SWS_Dcm_00793] [SWS_Dcm_91006].

If the application needs more time, the DCM transmits NRC 0x78 [SWS_Dcm_00024] to adhere to the time limits P2ServerMax and P2*ServerMax [SWS_Dcm_00027]. The number of such responses is limited and configurable [SWS_Dcm_00120] [SWS_Dcm_01567]. The application can also trigger NRC 0x78 itself: it returns DCM_E_FORCE_RCRRP and is called again after transmission confirmation [SWS_Dcm_00528] [SWS_Dcm_00529]. Memory callouts behave analogously [SWS_Dcm_00839].

Sequence diagram: Repeated call via OpStatus and the two paths to NRC 0x78. Sources: [SWS_Dcm_00530] [SWS_Dcm_00528] [SWS_Dcm_91015] SWS DCM p. 470

For InputOutputControlByIdentifier [SWS_Dcm_00256] with sender-receiver ports, the DCM writes the IOOperationRequest and evaluates the IOOperationResponse. DCM_RESPONSE_PENDING leads to NRC 0x78, a positive value leads to the positive response [SWS_Dcm_01441] [SWS_Dcm_01439] (SWS DCM p. 186).

Sessions, SecurityAccess, and communication modes

Session switches take place via service 0x10:

  • A non-configured session type leads to NRC 0x12 [SWS_Dcm_00307].
  • Only upon transmission confirmation does the DCM set the new session, the new P2 values, and the mode DcmDiagnosticSessionControl [SWS_Dcm_00311].
  • The S3Server timeout [SWS_Dcm_00140] or Dcm_ResetToDefaultSession [SWS_Dcm_00520] [SWS_Dcm_01062] leads back to the default session.
  • When switching to the default session, the DCM stops IO controls and periodic DIDs [SWS_Dcm_00628] [SWS_Dcm_01107].
  • When leaving a session, started ROE events transition to \"ROE stopped\" [SWS_Dcm_00879].
  • ComM is informed about active or inactive diagnostics [SWS_Dcm_01376] [SWS_Dcm_01377].

State diagram: Lifecycle of the diagnostic session with transitions and accompanying actions. Sources: [SWS_Dcm_00034] [SWS_Dcm_00311] [SWS_Dcm_00140] [SWS_Dcm_00520] SWS DCM p. 477

SecurityAccess (0x27) [SWS_Dcm_00252] proceeds in two steps:

  • requestSeed: If the requested level is already active, the DCM returns the seed 0x00 [SWS_Dcm_00323]. Otherwise, it calls Xxx_GetSeed [SWS_Dcm_00324].
  • sendKey: The DCM calls Xxx_CompareKey [SWS_Dcm_00324]. Upon E_OK, it sets the new level [SWS_Dcm_00325] and updates the mode DcmSecurityAccess [SWS_Dcm_01329].

Dcm_GetSecurityLevel returns the active level [SWS_Dcm_00338].

Sequence diagram: Seed/key procedure with failed attempt handling. Sources: [SWS_Dcm_00323] [SWS_Dcm_91003] [SWS_Dcm_91004] [SWS_Dcm_00660] [SWS_Dcm_01155]

ComM mode switches determine what DCM is allowed to send and receive:

  • Dcm_ComM_NoComModeEntered disables reception and transmission [SWS_Dcm_00148].
  • Dcm_ComM_SilentComModeEntered disables transmission, including ROE and periodic responses [SWS_Dcm_00153] [SWS_Dcm_00154] [SWS_Dcm_00155].
  • Dcm_ComM_FullComModeEntered enables everything [SWS_Dcm_00157].
  • ROE and periodic transmission take place only in Full Communication and do not wake up the bus [SWS_Dcm_00123] [SWS_Dcm_00126] [SWS_Dcm_00136].

State diagram: DCM transmit and receive permissions per ComM mode. Sources: [SWS_Dcm_00356] [SWS_Dcm_00358] [SWS_Dcm_00360] SWS DCM p. 478

Response On Event and Jump to Bootloader

Each ROE event has the states "cleared", "stopped", and "started" [SWS_Dcm_00871] (SWS DCM p. 61):

  • A valid setup leads to "stopped" [SWS_Dcm_00873].
  • startResponseOnEvent leads to "started" [SWS_Dcm_00876].
  • clearResponseOnEvent leads to "cleared" [SWS_Dcm_00875] [SWS_Dcm_00884].

An event is triggered by Dcm_TriggerOnEvent or Dcm_DemTriggerOnDTCStatus [SWS_Dcm_00920] [SWS_Dcm_00614]. The associated ServiceToRespondTo then executes like a normal request [SWS_Dcm_00922].

State diagram: Lifecycle of a RoeEvent. Sources: [SWS_Dcm_00872] [SWS_Dcm_00873] [SWS_Dcm_00876] [SWS_Dcm_00879] SWS DCM p. 61

If service 0x10 requests a session for an OEM or supplier bootloader [SWS_Dcm_00532] [SWS_Dcm_00592], the following sequence runs (SWS DCM p. 489):

  1. DCM passes the context (Dcm_ProgConditionsType) to Dcm_SetProgConditions [SWS_Dcm_00543] [SWS_Dcm_00988].
  2. On E_OK, it switches the mode DcmEcuReset [SWS_Dcm_00719].
  3. After the reset, Dcm_GetProgConditions reports via Dcm_EcuStartModeType whether a response is due [SWS_Dcm_00544] [SWS_Dcm_00987].

Sequence diagram: Jump to the bootloader and response after return. Interpretation: The user of DcmEcuReset triggers the reset. Sources: [SWS_Dcm_00720] [SWS_Dcm_01184] [SWS_Dcm_01181] [SWS_Dcm_00536] SWS DCM p. 489

Behavior in the event of an error

Errors are mostly translated into negative responses. Where no specific code is provided, DCM sends NRC 0x10 [SWS_Dcm_00271]. The individual cases:

  • Reception: In the event of Dcm_TpRxIndication with a result not equal to E_OK, DCM does not evaluate the data [SWS_Dcm_00344].
  • Transmission: After Dcm_TpTxConfirmation, DCM releases the transmit buffer and terminates timeout monitoring [SWS_Dcm_00352] [SWS_Dcm_00353] (ErrorDescription p. 26).
  • Application: E_NOT_OK or DCM_READ_FAILED leads to an NRC with the value from ErrorCode [SWS_Dcm_00678] [SWS_Dcm_00644]. The permitted value range and the handling of unexpected return values are specified separately [SWS_Dcm_01414] [SWS_Dcm_01415].
  • DEM: DEM_CLEAR_FAILED results in NRC 0x22, DEM_WRONG_DTC results in NRC 0x31, DEM_PENDING leads to a retry [SWS_Dcm_00704] [SWS_Dcm_00708] [SWS_Dcm_00703].
  • Concurrency: Higher-priority protocols preempt ongoing requests [SWS_Dcm_00015] [SWS_Dcm_00459]. If configured accordingly, rejected secondary requests receive NRC 0x21 [SWS_Dcm_00788] [SWS_Dcm_00789]. If Xxx_StartProtocol does not return E_OK, NRC 0x22 follows [SWS_Dcm_00674].
  • Security: As long as the delay timer is running, DCM responds negatively [SWS_Dcm_01350]. If reading the counter fails, the configured value applies [SWS_Dcm_01156].
  • Authentication: In case of idle state or S3Server timeout, the connection transitions to the "deauthenticated" state; role and whitelist are discarded [SWS_Dcm_01482] [SWS_Dcm_01483] [SWS_Dcm_01485] (SWS DCM p. 69).
  • Bootloader: If Dcm_SetProgConditions returns E_NOT_OK, no reset occurs; instead, DCM reports a DET error [SWS_Dcm_01181] [SWS_Dcm_01185].

Further detailed evidence

  • [SWS_Dcm_00094], [SWS_Dcm_00092], [SWS_Dcm_00351]: Transport interface to PduR.
  • [SWS_Dcm_00827], [SWS_Dcm_00211], [SWS_Dcm_00217]: Check chain of the DSD.
  • [SWS_Dcm_00984], [SWS_Dcm_00528]: OpStatus protocol and forced Response Pending.
  • [SWS_Dcm_00311], [SWS_Dcm_00140]: Session change.
  • [SWS_Dcm_00148], [SWS_Dcm_00157]: ComM coupling.
  • [SWS_Dcm_00543], [SWS_Dcm_00544]: Bootloader context.
  • SWS DCM p. 470: Process Busy Behavior (from R24-11, covered in content by [SWS_Dcm_00024]).

Diagnostic Communication Manager (DCM)

The DCM implements unified diagnostic services according to ISO 14229-1 (UDS) and ISO 15765-4 (OBD). It manages diagnostic sessions, security levels, and service routing.

function Dcm_Init [SWS_Dcm_00037] 📄 PDF

void Dcm_Init (const Dcm_ConfigType* ConfigPtr);

Service for basic initialization of DCM module.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: fd12917cfa80 Provenance

The synchronous and non-reentrant function Dcm_Init serves the fundamental initialization of the DCM module [SWS_Dcm_00037]. Via the parameter ConfigPtr, it accepts a pointer to the configuration set in post-build variants and has no return value [SWS_Dcm_00037]. During execution, the module initializes all global DCM variables with the values from the configuration [SWS_Dcm_00334].

As part of the initialization sequence, various functional areas and states are configured:

  • DDDID management: If the configuration parameter DcmDDDIDStorage is set to FALSE, the DCM initializes all dynamically defined data identifiers (DDDIDs) as not present during startup [SWS_Dcm_00866]. If the parameter is set to TRUE, the DDDID definitions are restored from the NvM [SWS_Dcm_00867].
  • Response on Event (ROE): The DCM transitions the state of each event during Dcm_Init into the status 'ROE cleared' [SWS_Dcm_00872].
  • Authentication status: If DcmDspAuthenticationPersistStateModeRuleRef is not configured or the referenced mode rule evaluates to false, the module sets all authentication states to the state 'deauthenticated' [SWS_Dcm_01480].
  • Communication status: After completion of Dcm_Init, the DCM sets the parameter ActiveDiagnostic to 'DCM_COMM_ACTIVE' [SWS_Dcm_01069].

Regarding the execution environment, it is specified that Dcm_Init is non-reentrant [SWS_Dcm_00037]. Specific error codes and standardized error messages to DET or DEM are not identified for this initialization service in the interface specification [SWS_Dcm_00037].

This usage note was generated automatically based on the AUTOSAR specification.

function Dcm_DemTriggerOnDTCStatus [SWS_Dcm_00614] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType Dcm_DemTriggerOnDTCStatus (uint32 DTC, Dem_UdsStatusByteType DTCStatusOld, Dem_UdsStatusByteType DTCStatusNew);

Triggers on changes of the UDS status byte. Allows to trigger on ROE Event for subservice On DTCStatusChanged.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 47d30a9a675c Provenance

use

The synchronous interface Dcm_DemTriggerOnDTCStatus (Service ID 0x2B) is available via the header Dcm_Dem.h and serves to report changes to the UDS status byte to the DCM [SWS_Dcm_00614]. This allows the DCM to trigger response-on-event (ROE) events for the diagnostic service subservice OnDTCStatusChanged [SWS_Dcm_00614]. When called, the function accepts three input parameters: the affected error code DTC (uint32), the previous state DTCStatusOld (Dem_UdsStatusByteType), and the updated state DTCStatusNew (Dem_UdsStatusByteType) [SWS_Dcm_00614]. Input/output parameters do not exist [SWS_Dcm_00614].

Return Values and Error Handling

As return value, the function provides the type Std_ReturnType, whereby according to the specification E_OK is returned without exception [SWS_Dcm_00614]. Specific error codes, fallback values, or separate notifications to DEM or DET are not indicated for this call.

Concurrency and Interaction

The function is classified as reentrant and possesses synchronous execution semantics [SWS_Dcm_00614]. Regarding interaction with diagnostic requests, a fixed constraint applies: If a request to clear the event memory (EventMemory) is currently being processed in the DCM, the DCM must ignore incoming calls of the callback Dcm_DemTriggerOnDTCStatus [SWS_Dcm_01410].

This usage note is based on the specifications of AUTOSAR Classic Release R20-11.

function Dcm_BndMWriteBlockFinish [SWS_Dcm_91088] 📄 PDF

void Dcm_BndMWriteBlockFinish (BndM_BlockIdType BlockId, BndM_ResultType result);

Called by BndM to indicate that a block write operation has finished.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: e13cfc7b4a9c Provenance

The function Dcm_BndMWriteBlockFinish serves as a notification interface from the BndM to the DCM to indicate the completion of a block write operation [SWS_Dcm_91088]. The function is declared in header file Dcm.h, has the service ID 0x7a, provides no return value (void), and is executed synchronously [SWS_Dcm_91088].

The interface expects two passing parameters [SWS_Dcm_91088]:

  • BlockId (type: BndM_BlockIdType): Identifies the block whose write operation has been completed.
  • result (type: BndM_ResultType): Transmits the result of the write operation to the DCM.

The functional interaction and the error handling behavior are coupled to atomic BndM write operations previously initiated by the DCM:

  • If Dcm_BndMWriteBlockFinish is called with status result = E_OK, the DCM sends a positive diagnostic response to the pending request [SWS_Dcm_01584].
  • If the function is called with result = E_NOT_OK, the DCM reacts with a negative diagnostic response 0x72 (generalProgrammingFailure) in case of an error [SWS_Dcm_01585].

Regarding concurrency, Dcm_BndMWriteBlockFinish is specified as non-reentrant (Non Reentrant) [SWS_Dcm_91088]. Callers must therefore ensure that the function is not called concurrently or preemptively by multiple contexts.

This usage note was generated by an AI and is based on the AUTOSAR specification R20-11.

function Dcm_SetDeauthenticatedRole [SWS_Dcm_91069] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType Dcm_SetDeauthenticatedRole (uint16 connectionId, Dcm_AuthenticationRoleType deauthenticatedRole);

Sets a new role used in deauthenticated state for that connection. The set role is valid until the connection switches into authenticated state or the ECU is reset.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 948c170851fe Provenance

Usage and Call Context

The function Dcm_SetDeauthenticatedRole is executed synchronously and reentrantly ([SWS_Dcm_91069]). It allows a software component to assign a new role deauthenticatedRole of type Dcm_AuthenticationRoleType for the deauthenticated state to a connection identified by connectionId ([SWS_Dcm_91069], [SWS_Dcm_01486]). The return value is invariably E_OK ([SWS_Dcm_91069]).

State Conditions and Error Handling

A call is processed by the DCM only if the connection is in the deauthenticated state (deauthenticated state) ([SWS_Dcm_01487]). Since the signature provides no alternative error values and always returns E_OK ([SWS_Dcm_91069]), a call outside this state is presumably discarded without an error message. Specific DET or DEM events are not defined in the specification.

Period of Validity and Lifecycle

If the role for the deauthenticated state is accepted successfully ([SWS_Dcm_01486]), this assignment persists temporarily:

  • The set role is discarded as soon as the connection transitions to the authenticated state (authenticated state) ([SWS_Dcm_01488]).
  • Validity ends at the latest upon a reset of the ECU ([SWS_Dcm_91069]).

function Dcm_GetSecurityLevel [SWS_Dcm_00338] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType Dcm_GetSecurityLevel (Dcm_SecLevelType* SecLevel);

This function provides the active security level value.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 7c05be541216 Provenance

The synchronous and reentrant function Dcm_GetSecurityLevel queries the currently active security level of the DCM and provides it [SWS_Dcm_00338]. The function is declared via the header Dcm.h and passes the determined status value to the caller via the output parameter SecLevel of type Dcm_SecLevelType*. According to the specification, E_OK is returned without exception [SWS_Dcm_00338].

The determination of the internal security level is based on the parameter SecurityAccessType transmitted by the tester as part of the service SecurityAccess according to the fixed conversion formula SecurityLevel = (SecurityAccessType + 1) / 2 [SWS_Dcm_00338].

In interaction with higher-level diagnostic service processing, the DSP submodule, among others, accesses this value: If the module receives a configured request with the subfunction type “requestSeed” (odd value) and the associated access level is already active according to Dcm_GetSecurityLevel, the DSP submodule sets the seed content to 0x00 [SWS_Dcm_00323].

Regarding concurrency and error handling, the function is defined as reentrant [SWS_Dcm_00338]. Since no specific error codes or DET checks are specified and E_OK is always returned, no null-pointer check is likely performed; callers must therefore presumably always pass a valid pointer to memory for SecLevel.

function Dcm_ResetToDefaultSession [SWS_Dcm_00520] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType Dcm_ResetToDefaultSession (void);

The call to this function allows the application to reset the current session to Default session. Example: Automatic termination of an extended diagnostic session upon exceeding of a speed limit.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 9e815ace4649 Provenance

The synchronous function Dcm_ResetToDefaultSession allows the application to reset the active diagnostic session to the default session [SWS_Dcm_00520]. A typical use case is the automatic termination of an extended diagnostic session as soon as a vehicle exceeds a predefined speed threshold [SWS_Dcm_00520].

Usage and Error Handling

  • Interface and parameters: The function is available via Dcm.h with service ID 0x2a, has the signature Std_ReturnType Dcm_ResetToDefaultSession (void), and requires no passed parameters [SWS_Dcm_00520].
  • Return value and errors: Std_ReturnType is returned as the return type, returning the value E_OK without exception [SWS_Dcm_00520]. Specific error codes, DET runtime checks, or DEM events are not specified in the requirements for this call.

Concurrency and Interaction

Execution is synchronous and declared as reentrant [SWS_Dcm_00520].

In addition to the actual session change, Dcm_ResetToDefaultSession mandatorily initiates a mode change for the ModeDeclarationGroupPrototype DcmDiagnosticSessionControl [SWS_Dcm_01062]. In doing so, the function internally calls SchM_Switch_<bsnp>_DcmDiagnosticSessionControl(RTE_MODE_DcmDiagnosticSessionControl_DCM_DEFAULT_SESSION) to notify the system environment about the transition to the default session [SWS_Dcm_01062].

function Dcm_TriggerOnEvent [SWS_Dcm_00521] 📄 PDF

Std_ReturnType Dcm_TriggerOnEvent (uint8 RoeEventId);

The call to this function allows to trigger an event linked to a ResponseOnEvent request. On the function call, the DCM will execute the associated service if the corresponding Mode of the Roe EventId is 'ROE started'.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 398801f84afa Provenance

The synchronous function Dcm_TriggerOnEvent (service ID 0x2D), provided via the header Dcm.h, serves to trigger an event linked to a ResponseOnEvent request (ROE) [SWS_Dcm_00521].

Call and Operation

The caller passes RoeEventId (input parameter of type uint8) as the only parameter, which identifies the event to be triggered; in/out or output parameters do not exist [SWS_Dcm_00521]. As soon as the function is called, the DCM checks the state of the event: if the passed RoeEvent is active, the DCM triggers the corresponding event [SWS_Dcm_00920]. The DCM executes the service associated with the event provided that the associated mode of the RoeEventId is set to 'ROE started' [SWS_Dcm_00521].

Return Values and Validation

The call synchronously returns a status of type Std_ReturnType providing information about the validity of the parameter [SWS_Dcm_00521]:

  • E_OK: The passed value for RoeEventId is valid [SWS_Dcm_00521].
  • E_NOT_OK: The value of RoeEventId is invalid [SWS_Dcm_00521].

Concurrency and Properties

The interface is specified as reentrant [SWS_Dcm_00521]. It can therefore be called concurrently to report events synchronously to the DCM [SWS_Dcm_00521].

function Dcm_StartOfReception [SWS_Dcm_00094] 📄 PDF

BufReq_ReturnType Dcm_StartOfReception (PduIdType id, const PduInfoType* info, PduLengthType TpSduLength, PduLengthType* bufferSizePtr);

This function is called at the start of receiving an N-SDU. The N-SDU might be fragmented into multiple N-PDUs (FF with one or more following CFs) or might consist of a single N-PDU (SF). The service shall provide the currently available maximum buffer size when invoked with TpSdu Length equal to 0. This function might be called in interrupt context.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: ab9eb5ff232f Provenance

The synchronous and reentrant function Dcm_StartOfReception ([SWS_Dcm_00094]) is called by a transport protocol module at the start of receiving an N-SDU—both for single frames (SF) and for segmented messages (First Frame, FF). It can be called in interrupt context ([SWS_Dcm_00094]). Among other things, the call causes the S3Server timer to stop at the start of reception ([SWS_Dcm_00141]).

Payload data and metadata are passed via info; for generic connections, this is used, among other things, to store SOURCE_ADDRESS_16 ([SWS_Dcm_00848]) and check TARGET_ADDRESS_16 ([SWS_Dcm_01347]). If neither payload nor metadata is present, NULL_PTR is passed ([SWS_Dcm_00094]). Via bufferSizePtr, the function reports back the available buffer for calculating the Block Size (BS) ([SWS_Dcm_00094]). Upon successful acceptance, it returns BUFREQ_OK, whereupon subsequent data is copied via Dcm_CopyRxData ([SWS_Dcm_00443]).

Error and rejection cases are signaled via the return value:

  • BUFREQ_E_OVFL: Returned if the requested length TpSduLength is greater than the buffer available in the DCM ([SWS_Dcm_00094], [SWS_Dcm_00444]). bufferSizePtr remains unchanged ([SWS_Dcm_00094]).
  • BUFREQ_E_NOT_OK: Returned if TpSduLength is equal to 0 ([SWS_Dcm_00642]) or an ongoing request on the same connection is blocking ([SWS_Dcm_00557]). For another connection, the parameter DcmDslDiagRespOnSecondDeclinedRequest decides whether it is rejected with BUFREQ_E_NOT_OK ([SWS_Dcm_00790]) or accepted with BUFREQ_OK ([SWS_Dcm_00788]). Concurrent TesterPresent requests are likewise acknowledged with BUFREQ_OK ([SWS_Dcm_00557]).

This function is called to provide the received data of an I-PDU segment (N-PDU) to the upper layer. Each call to this function provides the next part of the I-PDU data. The size of the remaining buffer is written to the position indicated by bufferSizePtr. This function might be called in interrupt context.

The synchronous function Dcm_CopyRxData is called to pass received data of an I-PDU segment (N-PDU) to the upper layer in the DCM [SWS_Dcm_00556]. Each call provides the next part of the I-PDU data [SWS_Dcm_00556]. The received I-PDU is identified via the parameter id [SWS_Dcm_00556]. The pointer info provides the source buffer via SduDataPtr and the number of bytes to be copied via SduLength [SWS_Dcm_00556]. After completion of the copy process, the remaining free buffer size in the DCM is returned via bufferSizePtr [SWS_Dcm_00556], [SWS_Dcm_00443].

If Dcm_CopyRxData is called with an SduLength of 0, this serves purely for buffer querying [SWS_Dcm_00556]. In this case, SduDataPtr may be a NULL_PTR; the function returns BUFREQ_OK and enters the remaining size of the receive buffer into bufferSizePtr [SWS_Dcm_00556], [SWS_Dcm_00996].

Interaction

Prior to copying, Dcm_StartOfReception must have been completed with BUFREQ_OK; subsequent calls of Dcm_CopyRxData copy the data from the provided buffer into the DCM buffer and update bufferSizePtr [SWS_Dcm_00443].

Error handling

The function returns the status as BufReq_ReturnType: BUFREQ_OK confirms the successful copying or the buffer query, while BUFREQ_E_NOT_OK indicates that no data was copied due to an error [SWS_Dcm_00556], [SWS_Dcm_00996].

Concurrency and Limitations

Dcm_CopyRxData is specified as reentrant and may be called in interrupt context [SWS_Dcm_00556]. The interface is provided via Dcm.h [SWS_Dcm_00556].

Usage and Call Context

The synchronous function Dcm_TpRxIndication is called after reception of an I-PDU via the TP API, typically by the module PduR [SWS_Dcm_00093], [SWS_Dcm_00112]. It passes the PDU identification (id) as well as the reception result (result) and returns no return value [SWS_Dcm_00093]. Since the function is reentrant and may be called in interrupt context, caller and module states must be designed for corresponding concurrency [SWS_Dcm_00093].

Behavior on Erroneous Reception

If Dcm_TpRxIndication is called with a result value that differs from E_OK, the module Dcm must not evaluate the buffer assigned to the referenced I-PDU [SWS_Dcm_00344].

Interaction of the Submodules

The DSL submodule forwards received data to the DSD submodule exclusively if the call was made with the parameter value result = E_OK [SWS_Dcm_00111]. Specific rules apply to diagnostic requests:

  • If the successfully received request (Result = E_OK) is the command TesterPresent with suppressPosRspMsgIndicationBit set (SID 0x3E, subfunction 0x80), the DSL submodule resets the session timeout timer S3Server [SWS_Dcm_00112].
  • In this case, the request is not forwarded by the DSL submodule to the DSD submodule for further interpretation [SWS_Dcm_00113].

function Dcm_CopyTxData [SWS_Dcm_00092] 📄 PDF

BufReq_ReturnType Dcm_CopyTxData (PduIdType id, const PduInfoType* info, const RetryInfoType* retry, PduLengthType* availableDataPtr);

This function is called to acquire the transmit data of an I-PDU segment (N-PDU). Each call to this function provides the next part of the I-PDU data unless retry->TpDataState is TP_ DATARETRY. In this case the function restarts to copy the data beginning at the offset from the current position indicated by retry->TxTpDataCnt. The size of the remaining data is written to the position indicated by availableDataPtr. This function might be called in interrupt context.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: a321989ea1cd Provenance

Usage and Semantics

The synchronous and reentrant function Dcm_CopyTxData is called by lower-layer modules (such as transport protocols) to retrieve data of an I-PDU segment (N-PDU) for transmission [SWS_Dcm_00092]. Via the parameter info, the caller passes the destination buffer SduDataPtr and the requested byte length SduLength. A value of 0 for SduLength can be used to signal status changes via retry or to query the amount of available data; in this case, SduDataPtr may be a NULL_PTR [SWS_Dcm_00092]. Via availableDataPtr, the DCM reports the remaining number of bytes in the transmit buffer, which can be used by TP modules to determine subsequent segment sizes and must not exceed the number of bytes still to be sent [SWS_Dcm_00092], [SWS_Dcm_00350].

Buffer Management and Transmission Retry

Acknowledgment or retry of data is controlled via the parameter retry [SWS_Dcm_00092]:

  • If retry is a NULL_PTR, the data may be removed from the buffer immediately after the copy process [SWS_Dcm_00092].
  • With TP_CONFPENDING, previously copied data must remain in the TP buffer for potential error recovery [SWS_Dcm_00092].
  • TP_DATACONF confirms all data copied prior to this call for release [SWS_Dcm_00092].
  • TP_DATARETRY recopies data starting from the offset TxTpDataCnt relative to the current position [SWS_Dcm_00092].

Return Values and Error Handling

If the data was copied successfully and completely, the function returns BUFREQ_OK [SWS_Dcm_00092], [SWS_Dcm_00346]. If not enough transmit data is available, no copy process is performed and BUFREQ_E_BUSY is returned; the lower layer can repeat the call later [SWS_Dcm_00092]. If the request fails, the function returns BUFREQ_E_NOT_OK [SWS_Dcm_00092]. In this case, the transmit request from PduR_DcmTransmit() is not yet completed; only a concluding call of Dcm_TpTxConfirmation terminates the process and enables new transmissions [SWS_Dcm_00350].

Concurrency

The function is reentrant and may also be called in interrupt context [SWS_Dcm_00092].

This usage note is based on the specifications of the AUTOSAR Classic Platform Release R20-11.

void Dcm_TpTxConfirmation (PduIdType id, Std_ReturnType result);

This function is called after the I-PDU has been transmitted on its network, the result indicates whether the transmission was successful or not. This function might be called in interrupt context.

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: e2141a66244b Provenance

The callback function Dcm_TpTxConfirmation ([SWS_Dcm_00351]) is called synchronously by the lower transport layer after a diagnostic I-PDU has been transmitted on the network. The affected I-PDU is identified via the parameter id, while result reports the success or failure of the transmission process ([SWS_Dcm_00351]). The function has no return value, is reentrant, and may explicitly be executed in interrupt context ([SWS_Dcm_00351]).

When Dcm_TpTxConfirmation is called, the DCM module performs central cleanup and state transitions:

  • The assigned transmit buffer is unlocked ([SWS_Dcm_00352]).
  • Running error monitorings such as page buffer timeouts as well as P2ServerMax and P2*ServerMax timeouts are stopped ([SWS_Dcm_00353]).
  • The DcmPduId of the connection, which had been locked since reception (Dcm_TpRxIndication), is released so that subsequent requests can be received ([SWS_Dcm_00241]).
  • The active protocol is not terminated by the confirmation of the DSL response (no call of xxx_StopProtocol) ([SWS_Dcm_00624]).

In the event of an error (if result indicates an error or an abort after a failed Dcm_CopyTxData is confirmed), [SWS_Dcm_00350] mandatorily requires this final call in order to formally conclude the transmission order and enable new transmissions via PduR_DcmTransmit(). Upon an erroneous confirmation, the DSD submodule must not retransmit the diagnostic response ([SWS_Dcm_00118]).

In addition, confirmation of a response (other than NRC 0x78) marks the regular completion of a diagnostic request ([SWS_Dcm_01378]). Following confirmation of a positive response to a EcuReset, the DCM ignores all further requests during reset processing ([SWS_Dcm_00834]).

According to [SWS_Dcm_01092], the synchronous interface Dcm_TxConfirmation (service ID 0x40, declared in Dcm.h) is called by the underlying communication interface module to confirm the transmission of a PDU or to report the failure of the transmission. The function has no return value and processes two input parameters:

  • TxPduId: Identifier (PduIdType) of the transmitted PDU.
  • result: Status of the transmission (Std_ReturnType). Valid values are E_OK in the case of successful transmission and E_NOT_OK if the transmission of the PDU failed.

The result of the transmission is signaled directly to the DCM via the parameter result ([SWS_Dcm_01092]). Specific DET or DEM error messages are not defined for this function in the provided specification excerpt.

Regarding reentrancy, Dcm_TxConfirmation is reentrant for calls with different PDU IDs, but not reentrant for the same TxPduId ([SWS_Dcm_01092]). It should be noted that the call by the underlying module can take place in the interrupt context ([SWS_Dcm_01092]).

Interaction

In the case of a periodic transmission (PeriodicTransmission), the DCM is called according to [SWS_Dcm_01073] via Dcm_TxConfirmation to be notified of the respective transmission result.

The synchronous and reentrant function Dcm_ComM_NoComModeEntered (service ID 0x21) informs the DCM module about the transition of a communication network to the state COMM_NO_COMMUNICATION [SWS_Dcm_00356]. The interface is provided via the header Dcm_ComM.h, has no return value, and identifies the affected network via the input parameter NetworkId of type uint8 [SWS_Dcm_00356].

With this call, the DCM shuts down any communication on the specified network, completely disabling both reception and transmission of messages [SWS_Dcm_00148]. This mandatorily includes the following transmission types:

  • suppression of ResponseOnEvent transmissions [SWS_Dcm_00149],
  • deactivation of periodic transmissions via ReadDataByPeriodicIdentifier (periodicId) [SWS_Dcm_00150], and
  • shutdown of normal transmissions [SWS_Dcm_00151].

Consequently, following execution of Dcm_ComM_NoComModeEntered, the DCM module must no longer call the PduR function PduR_DcmTransmit() for this context [SWS_Dcm_00152].

If the function is called with a NetworkId that does not correspond to any ComM channel referenced in the DCM via configuration parameter DcmDslProtocolComMChannelRef, the DCM module does not perform any actions and returns immediately [SWS_Dcm_01324].

Usage and Semantics

The synchronous and reentrant callback function Dcm_CsmAsyncJobFinished is called by the Crypto Service Manager (CSM) as soon as asynchronous job processing is completed [SWS_Dcm_91076]. As an input parameter, it receives the result of the finished CSM job via result of type Csm_ResultType [SWS_Dcm_91076]. As a return value, the function always returns E_OK [SWS_Dcm_91076].

Configuration and Constraints

Integrators must configure the name of this function in the ECUC configuration of the CSM as a callback for asynchronous jobs [SWS_Dcm_91076]. For the DCM, only a single such callback is available; according to the specification, identification of the finished job takes place by evaluating the job parameter [SWS_Dcm_91076]. However, since the C function signature only passes result, the DCM is likely to determine the associated job internally via the transaction state of the ongoing authentication.

The interface is only available if the parameter DcmDspAuthenticationConnection is set in the configuration (not equal to null) [SWS_Dcm_91076]. Specific error handlings or DET messages are not specified for this call, since the return value is unalterably E_OK [SWS_Dcm_91076].

The callout function Dcm_ReadMemory ([SWS_Dcm_00539]), declared in Dcm_Externals.h, serves the DCM for reading server memory data based on start address (MemoryAddress) and byte size (MemorySize). The function is required for the UDS services ReadMemoryByAddress (0x23) ([SWS_Dcm_00495]), ReadDataByIdentifier (0x22) for dynamic DIDs in the address range 0xF200 to 0xF3FF ([SWS_Dcm_00653]), RequestUpload, and TransferData ([SWS_Dcm_00539]). If the parameter MemoryIdentifier is not used, it must be set to 0 ([SWS_Dcm_00539]).

The interface is asynchronous and non-reentrant ([SWS_Dcm_00539]). The call status is passed via OpStatus with the values DCM_INITIAL, DCM_PENDING, DCM_CANCEL, or DCM_FORCE_RCRRP_OK. As long as the read operation is in progress, the function returns DCM_READ_PENDING ([SWS_Dcm_00985]). If the call returns DCM_READ_FORCE_RCRRP, the DCM immediately initiates transmission of an RCR-RP message (NRC 0x78) and pauses further calls until transmission confirmation ([SWS_Dcm_00839]). After confirmation of the RCR-RP, the DCM calls the function from Dcm_MainFunction again with OpStatus = DCM_FORCE_RCRRP_OK ([SWS_Dcm_00840]).

In case of success, the read data is written to buffer MemoryData and DCM_READ_OK is returned ([SWS_Dcm_00539], [SWS_Dcm_00985]). If the operation fails, the function returns DCM_READ_FAILED and sets ErrorCode. The DCM then sends a negative response with the corresponding NRC value ([SWS_Dcm_00644]).

The callout function Dcm_SetProgConditions enables the integrator to persistently save relevant information before transitioning to the bootloader or performing a reset as a result of an ECUReset request [SWS_Dcm_00543]. The relevant context data is passed via a pointer to structure Dcm_ProgConditionsType, which bundles, among other things, connection and tester source addresses, service and sub-function IDs, as well as control flags such as ReprogramingRequest and ResponseRequired [SWS_Dcm_00988]. Upon receipt of a UDS service 0x10 with sub-function 0x02, the DCM sets these flags and calls the interface [SWS_Dcm_01182].

The call is asynchronous and non-reentrant (Non Reentrant) [SWS_Dcm_00543]. The states DCM_INITIAL, DCM_PENDING, DCM_CANCEL, or DCM_FORCE_RCRRP_OK are controlled via parameter OpStatus [SWS_Dcm_00543]. If execution is ongoing and the function returns DCM_E_PENDING, the DCM calls the interface again in the next main function cycle to complete the setting [SWS_Dcm_00543], [SWS_Dcm_01184]. By means of DCM_E_FORCE_RCRRP, the transmission of a response pending reply (NRC 0x78) can be forced [SWS_Dcm_00543]. Depending on the configuration, the call by the DCM takes place only after successful transmission of NRC 0x78 [SWS_Dcm_00535].

If the conditions were set without errors and the callout returns E_OK, the DCM initiates the mode switch of ModeDeclarationGroupPrototype DcmEcuReset to EXECUTE [SWS_Dcm_00719], [SWS_Dcm_01163], [SWS_Dcm_01180]. If, on the other hand, the state cannot be saved and the function responds with E_NOT_OK, the reset as well as the bootloader jump are omitted, the mode switch is prevented, and the DCM sends the negative response NRC 0x22 (Conditions not correct) [SWS_Dcm_00715], [SWS_Dcm_01181].

The function Dcm_MainFunction serves to process the central tasks of the main loop of the Diagnostic Communication Manager ([SWS_Dcm_00053]). It has the signature void Dcm_MainFunction(void) and provides no return values. Since it is provided via the header SchM_Dcm.h, its invocation likely occurs cyclically in the context of a basic software scheduler task.

An essential task is the control and cross-cycle continuation of asynchronous processes:

  • If an operation with Dcm_OpStatusType returns the return value DCM_E_PENDING, the DCM invokes the operation again with OpStatus = DCM_PENDING upon every call of Dcm_MainFunction as long as this status persists ([SWS_Dcm_00530]).
  • If Dem_ClearDTC() returns the status DEM_PENDING, the function is called again in the next cycle of Dcm_MainFunction; the DCM sends NRC 78 (ResponsePending) if necessary ([SWS_Dcm_00703]).
  • Calls of Dem_SetDTCFilter() with parameter FilterForFault-DetectionCounter set must imperatively take place in the context of Dcm_MainFunction ([SWS_Dcm_00519]).
  • After confirmation of an RCR-RP transmission, the DCM calls operations such as Dcm_WriteMemory or Dcm_ReadMemory from Dcm_MainFunction again with OpStatus = DCM_FORCE_RCRRP_OK ([SWS_Dcm_00529], [SWS_Dcm_00838], [SWS_Dcm_00840]).
  • If the value DCM_E_PENDING is reported for Xxx_GetSecurityAttemptCounter, the call is interrupted and resumed in the next cycle ([SWS_Dcm_01351]); if the configured timeout is exceeded, the DCM aborts the pending operation with OpStatus = DCM_CANCEL ([SWS_Dcm_01352]).

It is called as soon as a UDS request of the service SecurityAccess (0x27) with the subfunction type "requestSeed" is received and the requested security level is not yet active [SWS_Dcm_00862], [SWS_Dcm_00324].

Call Context and Parameters

The interface is defined as non-reentrant (Non Reentrant) and operates asynchronously [SWS_Dcm_01151]:

  • SecurityAccessDataRecord: Pointer to additional input data for the seed calculation; the minimum size is one byte according to DcmDspSecurityADRSize [SWS_Dcm_01151].

  • ErrorCode: Output parameter for returning a negative error code (NRC) [SWS_Dcm_01151].

Return Values and Error Handling

  • E_OK: The seed was successfully determined and provided [SWS_Dcm_01151].
  • DCM_E_PENDING: The calculation is not yet completed; subsequent calculations or calls are necessary for completion [SWS_Dcm_01151].
  • E_NOT_OK: The request failed. In this case, the DCM module sends a negative UDS response with the NRC value passed in the parameter ErrorCode [SWS_Dcm_01151], [SWS_Dcm_00659].

Depending on the configuration of DcmDspSecurityUsePort, the connection is established as a C function in USE_ASYNCH_FNC (referenced via DcmDspSecurityGetSeedFnc) [SWS_Dcm_00862] or as an Rte operation in USE_ASYNCH_CLIENT_SERVER [SWS_Dcm_00324]. The function Xxx_CompareKey is called asynchronously and non-reentrantly by the Diagnostic Communication Manager ([SWS_Dcm_91004]) to compare a received key against the internal logic of the application within the scope of the UDS service SecurityAccess (0x27, subfunction sendKey) ([SWS_Dcm_00863]). It is used when the access status is not yet active, the seed request was successful, and the configuration parameter DcmDspSecurityUsePort is set to USE_ASYNCH_CLIENT_SERVER ([SWS_Dcm_00324]) or, according to [SWS_Dcm_00863], the function interface was configured via USE_ASYNCH_FNC/DcmDspSecurityCompareKeyFnc. The interface is declared in Dcm_Externals.h ([SWS_Dcm_91004]).

The passed arguments comprise the pointer to the key to be checked Key, the current operation status OpStatus (of type Dcm_OpStatusType), and the pointer ErrorCode for the negative response code to be output in case of an error ([SWS_Dcm_91004]). The following return values are specified:

  • E_OK: Key verification successful ([SWS_Dcm_91004]).
  • DCM_E_PENDING: Verification not yet completed; further calls by the DCM module are required for completion ([SWS_Dcm_91004]).
  • E_NOT_OK: Processing not successful. The DCM then sends a negative UDS response with the NRC set in ErrorCode without changing the internal security level or incrementing the attempt counter (AttemptCounter) ([SWS_Dcm_01150]).
  • DCM_E_COMPARE_KEY_FAILED: Key does not match ([SWS_Dcm_91004]).

If the key comparison fails (DCM_E_COMPARE_KEY_FAILED) and DcmDspSecurityNumAttDelay is configured, the AttemptCounter is incremented ([SWS_Dcm_01397]). If the counter is below the limit, the DCM sends NRC 0x35 (InvalidKey) ([SWS_Dcm_00660]). If the number of failed attempts reaches or exceeds the configured limit DcmDspSecurityNumAttDelay, the DCM starts the SecurityDelayTimer with duration DcmDspSecurityDelayTime and sends NRC 0x36 (exceededNumberOfAttempts) ([SWS_Dcm_01349]). In both cases, the security level remains unchanged.

During the initialization of the DCM, the asynchronous and non-reentrant function [SWS_Dcm_01152] reads the current failed attempt counter for a configured security level from the application. The call is made for each entry in DcmDspSecurityRow for which the configuration parameter DcmDspSecurityAttemptCounterEnabled is set to TRUE [SWS_Dcm_01154].

Flow control is managed via the parameter OpStatus with the values DCM_INITIAL, DCM_PENDING, or DCM_CANCEL [SWS_Dcm_01152]. If the function returns DCM_E_PENDING, the DCM interrupts the call chain and resumes it in the subsequent cycle of Dcm_MainFunction() [SWS_Dcm_01351]. If the timeout DcmDspSecurityMaxAttemptCounterReadoutTime configured after the first cycle is exceeded, the DCM aborts the still pending process with DCM_CANCEL [SWS_Dcm_01352].

In case of success, the interface returns E_OK and passes the counter value via the output parameter AttemptCounter [SWS_Dcm_01152]. If the call returns E_NOT_OK, the DCM automatically sets the counter to the value configured for this security level DcmDspSecurityNumAttDelay [SWS_Dcm_01156].

As long as not all counter values have been definitively determined or aborted, the DCM rejects any request for SecurityAccess (0x27) to request a seed with the negative response code conditionsNotCorrect (0x22) [SWS_Dcm_01354]. After completion of the query chain, the DCM checks the counter values: If at least one counter reaches or exceeds the threshold value DcmDspSecurityNumAttDelay, the DCM starts the SecurityDelayTimer with the higher value of DcmDspSecurityDelayTimeOnBoot and DcmDspSecurityDelayTime [SWS_Dcm_01355].

The callback function Xxx_StartProtocol is provided via the header Dcm_Externals.h and allows the application, upon the first request of a diagnostic protocol, to check current environmental conditions and to enable or reject further protocol processing [SWS_Dcm_01339].

Call Context and Parameters

The call is performed by the DSL submodule of the DCM synchronously and non-reentrantly for all configured functions [SWS_Dcm_00036], [SWS_Dcm_01339]. The following input parameters are passed to the function [SWS_Dcm_01339]:

  • ProtocolType: Type of the diagnostic protocol to be started,
  • TesterSourceAddress: Source address of the requesting tester,
  • ConnectionId: Unique identifier of the connection.

Return Values and Error Handling

As a return value, the function returns Std_ReturnType with E_OK upon successful release, E_NOT_OK if the check was unsuccessful, or E_PROTOCOL_NOT_ALLOWED if the protocol is invalid [SWS_Dcm_01339]. If at least one configured Xxx_StartProtocol function does not return E_OK, the DCM aborts protocol start and responds with NRC 0x22 [SWS_Dcm_00674].

Initialization after Successful Release

Only after all configured Xxx_StartProtocol callbacks have returned E_OK does the DCM execute the further initialization steps:

  • Loading of the standard timing parameters from the default session configuration [SWS_Dcm_00144],
  • Activation of the service table [SWS_Dcm_00145],
  • Resetting of the security status (Security State) [SWS_Dcm_00146],
  • Resetting of the session status to the default diagnostic session as well as executing the mode switch via SchM_Switch_<bsnp>_DcmDiagnosticSessionControl to RTE_MODE_DcmDiagnosticSessionControl_DEFAULT_SESSION [SWS_Dcm_00147].

The synchronous, non-reentrant function Xxx_Indication is declared via the header Dcm_Externals.h [SWS_Dcm_01341]. It indicates the impending execution of a diagnostic service to the application and allows it to reject the execution of the service request [SWS_Dcm_01341]. The call is made synchronously by the DSD submodule at all configured ServiceRequestIndication ports if the configuration containers DcmDsdServiceRequestManufacturerNotification [SWS_Dcm_00218] or DcmDsdServiceRequestSupplierNotification [SWS_Dcm_00516] are present.

The service ID (SID), the request data without SID (RequestData, DataSize), the addressing type (ReqType), the connection ID (ConnectionId), the protocol type (ProtocolType), and the source address of the tester (TesterSourceAddress) are passed as input parameters [SWS_Dcm_01341].

Via the return value of type Std_ReturnType, the application controls the response of the DSD submodule [SWS_Dcm_01341]:

  • E_OK: The request was successful and is processed further normally [SWS_Dcm_01341].
  • E_REQUEST_NOT_ACCEPTED: The request is not accepted. If at least one called indication function returns E_REQUEST_NOT_ACCEPTED, the DSD submodule suppresses any response to the tester [SWS_Dcm_00462], [SWS_Dcm_00517].
  • E_NOT_OK: The request was not successful. In this case, the application writes a negative response code to the output parameter ErrorCode [SWS_Dcm_01341]. Provided that no call returns E_REQUEST_NOT_ACCEPTED, the DSD submodule sends a negative response with this NRC [SWS_Dcm_00463], [SWS_Dcm_00518].

If multiple functions return E_NOT_OK and no function returns E_REQUEST_NOT_ACCEPTED when multiple notifications are configured, the DSD submodule mandatorily uses the ErrorCode of the first function responding with E_NOT_OK for the negative response [SWS_Dcm_01321], [SWS_Dcm_01322].

The callback function Xxx_Confirmation serves to synchronously notify the application of the completion of a diagnostic transmission—either the successful transmission or a transmission error ([SWS_Dcm_01342]). The declaration is provided via the header Dcm_Externals.h ([SWS_Dcm_01342]).

When called by the DCM submodule DSD (Diagnostic Service Dispatcher), essential context data of the diagnostic order is passed ([SWS_Dcm_01342], [SWS_Dcm_00741]):

  • SID: Identifier of the diagnostic service ([SWS_Dcm_01342]).
  • ReqType: Addressing type (0 for physical, 1 for functional) ([SWS_Dcm_01342]).
  • ConnectionId, ProtocolType, and TesterSourceAddress: Unique connection and protocol attributes as well as the source address of the tester ([SWS_Dcm_01342]).
  • ConfirmationStatus: Status information about the success or error of the transmission ([SWS_Dcm_01342]).

The operation returns Std_ReturnType as return value (E_OK upon successful confirmation processing, otherwise E_NOT_OK) ([SWS_Dcm_01342]). The DSD calls the function on all ports that use the interface ServiceRequestNotification (configured via DcmDsdServiceRequestManufacturerNotification or DcmDsdServiceRequestSupplierNotification) ([SWS_Dcm_00741]).

Regarding the call sequence, Xxx_Confirmation is regularly executed directly after DspInternal_DcmConfirmation() ([SWS_Dcm_00742]). However, if the special case according to [SWS_Dcm_01172] applies, the DSD exclusively calls Xxx_Confirmation, while the internal call is omitted.

Since Xxx_Confirmation is specified as non-reentrant (Non Reentrant) and synchronous ([SWS_Dcm_01342]), the application-side implementation should presumably contain no blocking processes and trigger no reentrant callbacks into the DCM (interpretation).

The callout function Xxx_ProcessRequestDownload ([SWS_Dcm_00754]) is called by the module Dcm to initiate a download process during processing of the UDS service RequestDownload. It is defined as asynchronous and non-reentrant and is provided via the header Dcm_Externals.h ([SWS_Dcm_00754]).

Usage and Parameters

The call takes place step by step via the parameter OpStatus with the values DCM_INITIAL, DCM_PENDING, or DCM_CANCEL ([SWS_Dcm_00754]). The compression and encryption methods (DataFormatIdentifier), the memory block (MemoryIdentifier), the start address (MemoryAddress), and the uncompressed memory size in bytes (MemorySize) are passed as input parameters ([SWS_Dcm_00754]). Prior to the call, the Dcm writes the maximum possible buffer size to the inout parameter BlockLength ([SWS_Dcm_01417]). The function adjusts this value to the maximum permissible block length for subsequent write operations ([SWS_Dcm_00754]).

Return Values and Interaction

The function returns E_OK upon successful execution, DCM_E_PENDING if processing is still ongoing, or E_NOT_OK in the event of an error ([SWS_Dcm_00754]):

  • If the call returns E_OK and the negotiated value BlockLength is less than or equal to the supported buffer length of the current protocol connection, the Dcm sends a positive response with this value as maxNumberOfBlockLength ([SWS_Dcm_01419]).
  • If the returned buffer length exceeds the supported buffer size of the protocol connection, the Dcm reports the DET error DCM_E_INTERFACE_BUFFER_OVERFLOW ([SWS_Dcm_01418]).
  • Upon return of E_NOT_OK, the Dcm sends a negative UDS response (NRC) with the value set in the output parameter ErrorCode ([SWS_Dcm_00754], [SWS_Dcm_00757]).

The return value of type Dcm_ReturnWriteMemoryType signals the result of the operation [SWS_Dcm_91071]:

  • DCM_WRITE_OK: Write operation completed successfully [SWS_Dcm_91071].
  • DCM_WRITE_PENDING: Write operation is not yet completed [SWS_Dcm_91071].
  • DCM_WRITE_FORCE_RCRRP: Write operation is still pending; transmission of the pending response (Response Pending) starts immediately [SWS_Dcm_91071].
  • DCM_WRITE_FAILED: Write operation failed [SWS_Dcm_91071].

If the callout returns the value DCM_WRITE_FAILED, the DCM module sends a negative response with the NRC value passed in parameter ErrorCode [SWS_Dcm_91071]. The callout is specified as non-reentrant (Non Reentrant) and must therefore not be executed concurrently [SWS_Dcm_91071].

The data type Dcm_CommunicationModeType is an enumeration type declared in Dcm.h based on uint8 ([SWS_Dcm_00981]). It defines the communication modes for selectively controlling the transmission (Tx) and reception (Rx) paths. The value range comprises the values 0x00 to 0x0B for normal application data (NORM), network management (NM), and both communication branches combined (NORM_NM) ([SWS_Dcm_00981]).

The type is used as a parameter in calls to the BSW interface BswM_Dcm_CommunicationMode_CurrentState. Via this interface, the DCM forwards the current mode to the BSW Mode Manager after confirmation (Sent Confirmation) of a UDS service request CommunicationControl (Service 0x28) ([SWS_Dcm_00512], [SWS_Dcm_00785]). The specific mode value corresponds to the parameters communicationType and controlType of the received diagnostic request ([SWS_Dcm_00512]).

The interaction and the affected networks depend on the subnet parameter of the UDS request:

  • For subnet 0x00, the update is performed for all network channels configured in DcmDspComControlAllChannel ([SWS_Dcm_00512]).
  • For subnet 0x0F, the communication mode of the current diagnostic reception channel is reported ([SWS_Dcm_00785]).
  • For subnets from 0x01 to 0x0E, support is checked; unsupported subnets are rejected with the negative response code 0x31 ([SWS_Dcm_00786]).
  • For subfunctions with enhanced addressing (such as enableRxAndDisableTxWithEnhancedAddressInformation or enableRxAndTxWithEnhancedAddressInformation), the call is made for the channel referenced via the sub-node ID ([SWS_Dcm_01077], [SWS_Dcm_01079]).

Usage and Type Definition

The data type Dcm_MsgType is the central pointer type for diagnostic messages in the Diagnostic Communication Manager and is available via the header Dcm.h [SWS_Dcm_00990]. It is declared as a pointer to Dcm_MsgItemType* and serves as a common basis for referencing requests as well as positive and negative response messages [SWS_Dcm_00990]. Interpretation: Since the base type Dcm_MsgItemType is not detailed further in the specification, it is likely to typically represent a single data byte (such as uint8) through which the linear message buffer is accessed sequentially.

Interplay and Structure Context

The primary use of Dcm_MsgType occurs within the context structure Dcm_MsgContextType [SWS_Dcm_00994]. There, the type references two separate data areas:

  • reqData: Points to the payload data of the diagnostic request, beginning immediately after the service identifier (SID), which itself is not part of this data [SWS_Dcm_00994].
  • resData: Points to the data of a positive response and likewise begins immediately after the service identifier [SWS_Dcm_00994].

Buffer Limits and Constraints

When processing and populating the response buffers addressed via Dcm_MsgType, users must strictly adhere to the associated buffer limits [SWS_Dcm_00994]. The actual response length resDataLen must under no circumstances exceed the buffer capacity defined by resMaxDataLen, since the maximum response size is strictly limited by the allocation of the assigned buffer [SWS_Dcm_00994].

The data type Dcm_MsgLenType is available via the header Dcm.h and derived from the base type uint32 [SWS_Dcm_00991]. It is used in the Diagnostic Communication Manager (DCM) to describe the length of diagnostic messages. This includes both diagnostic requests and positive and negative response messages (responses) [SWS_Dcm_00991].

Regarding the value range limits, the specification defines that the maximum transmittable length of a diagnostic message depends on the respective underlying transport protocol or transmission medium [SWS_Dcm_00991]. Interpretation: Although the underlying data type uint32 can represent message lengths of up to 4 GiB on the software side, the actual maximum length in practice is likely to always be limited by the communication medium and the buffer sizes.

Dcm_MsgLenType plays a central role in the structure Dcm_MsgContextType, which encapsulates the context of a diagnostic job [SWS_Dcm_00994]. Within this structure, it typifies several fundamental length specifications:

  • reqDataLen: Represents the length of the request data. Counting begins immediately after the service identifier, so that it is not included in the length specification [SWS_Dcm_00994].
  • resDataLen: Specifies the length of the positive response data, likewise excluding the service identifier [SWS_Dcm_00994].
  • resMaxDataLen: Specifies the maximum possible length of a response, which is limited by the size of the allocated buffer [SWS_Dcm_00994].

When implementing service handlers, strict care must therefore be taken to ensure that length calculations for reqDataLen and resDataLen are always performed without the service identifier and that response data does not exceed the buffer limit specified by resMaxDataLen [SWS_Dcm_00994].

The data structure Dcm_MsgContextType provides all necessary information to control a diagnostic request from processing through response to confirmation [SWS_Dcm_00994]. When using it, the following aspects must be observed:

  • Response length and error case: If the generated response length exceeds the buffer limit defined via protocol-dependent field resMaxDataLen and DcmPagedBufferEnabled == FALSE holds, the DCM responds with the negative response code 0x14 (DCM_E_RESPONSETOOLONG) [SWS_Dcm_01059]. If processing in the service handler fails, the application reports back E_NOT_OK with an error code [SWS_Dcm_00763].
  • Additional information and response suppression: Among other things, suppressPosRspMsgIndicationBit is transported via msgAddInfo; if this is set, the DSD suppresses positive responses [SWS_Dcm_00202], [SWS_Dcm_00231].
  • Lifetime and context assignment: Upon reaching confirmation, the structure loses its validity and all message data is lost [SWS_Dcm_00994]. Applications must already save identifier idContext at request start in order to associate a subsequent confirmation with the original request [SWS_Dcm_00994].
  • Protocol reference: Field dcmRxPduId identifies the receive PDU and allows differentiated handling depending on the diagnostic protocol, for example between OBD and enhanced diagnostics [SWS_Dcm_00994].

Interpretation: Since the context becomes invalid at confirmation, the underlying memory buffer is likely released or overwritten immediately by the DSL for subsequent communications after transmission of the response.

It controls the execution and lifecycle state of asynchronous diagnostic operations of the Diagnostic Communication Manager (DCM), such as Dcm_ReadMemory [SWS_Dcm_00539], Dcm_WriteMemory [SWS_Dcm_00540], or Dcm_SetProgConditions [SWS_Dcm_00543].

Four status values are defined for controlling the operation flow [SWS_Dcm_00984]:

  • DCM_PENDING (0x01): Signals a subsequent call after previously returning a pending state [SWS_Dcm_00984]. If an operation returns the error value DCM_E_PENDING, the DCM calls this operation again with OpStatus = DCM_PENDING in each subsequent cycle of Dcm_MainFunction until processing is completed [SWS_Dcm_00530].
  • DCM_CANCEL (0x02): Explicitly requests the called entity to cancel a still pending asynchronous operation [SWS_Dcm_00984].
  • DCM_FORCE_RCRRP_OK (0x03): Confirms that a response-pending message (NRC 0x78) has been transmitted [SWS_Dcm_00984]. If the operation replies with DCM_E_FORCE_RCRRP, the DCM initiates the sending of RCR-RP and suspends further calls to the operation until sending is completed [SWS_Dcm_00528].

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 63d2c6367edd Provenance

Usage and Value Range

The data type Dcm_ConfirmationStatusType is an enumeration type derived from uint8, provided via the header file Rte_Dcm_Type.h [SWS_Dcm_00983]. It is used to report the status of a transmitted diagnostic response—both in the event of successful transmission and in the event of transmission errors—to the application or internal service handlers [SWS_Dcm_01342]. The value range comprises four discrete states [SWS_Dcm_00983]:

  • DCM_RES_POS_OK (0x00): Interpretation: The positive diagnostic response was successfully transmitted.
  • DCM_RES_POS_NOT_OK (0x01): Interpretation: An error occurred during the transmission of the positive diagnostic response.
  • DCM_RES_NEG_OK (0x02): Interpretation: The negative diagnostic response (NRC) was successfully transmitted.
  • DCM_RES_NEG_NOT_OK (0x03): Interpretation: An error occurred during the transmission of the negative diagnostic response.

Interaction and Interfaces

The confirmation status is passed as an input parameter (IN) in synchronous callback functions. In the generic confirmation interface Xxx_Confirmation, the parameter is transmitted together with the service identifier (SID), addressing type (ReqType), connection ID (ConnectionId), protocol type, and tester source address [SWS_Dcm_01342]. Interface ServiceRequestNotification also integrates this status via operation Confirmation [SWS_Dcm_00694].

During the execution of routine services, the type is used specifically to report back the transmission status after completion of individual routine operations. The callbacks Xxx_StartConfirmation [SWS_Dcm_91016], Xxx_StopConfirmation [SWS_Dcm_91017], and Xxx_RequestResultsConfirmation [SWS_Dcm_91018] declared in Dcm_Externals.h serve this purpose.

Concurrency and Execution

The confirmation functions return a Std_ReturnType (e.g. E_OK or E_NOT_OK) [SWS_Dcm_01342], [SWS_Dcm_91016]. All mentioned interface calls are executed synchronously and are declared as non-reentrant (Non Reentrant) [SWS_Dcm_01342], [SWS_Dcm_91016], [SWS_Dcm_91017], [SWS_Dcm_91018].

According to [SWS_Dcm_91035], the interface ModeRapidPowerShutDownModeSwitchInterface is specified as PPortPrototype (ProvidedPort) for the interface Dcm_ModeRapidPowerShutDownModeSwitchInterface in module Dcm. It serves to notify software components (SW-Cs) about the rapid power shut down mode (Rapid Power Shut Down Mode).

Regarding usage, behavior, and interaction, the following aspects are relevant:

  • Usage and semantics: Via the ModeSwitchInterface, the DCM signals mode switches to connected SW-Cs. The call context lies within the DCM module, which initiates the mode change; transmission to the receivers occurs asynchronously via the RTE [SWS_Dcm_91035].
  • Error handling: The port definition does not contain any specific error codes, return values, or DET/DEM events. Errors during mode transmission are therefore likely to be completely intercepted by the standard mechanisms of the AUTOSAR RTE for mode-switch ports.
  • Concurrency and restrictions: Notification takes place in the execution context of the DCM. Receiving SW-Cs are presumably activated via mode-triggered runnables and must be designed in such a way that they execute the actions for rapid power shutdown without blocking delays.

type ControlDTCSettingModeSwitchInterface [SWS_Dcm_91037] 📄 PDF

A ModeSwitchInterface PPortPrototype used to notify SW-Cs about the DTC Setting mode

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 0b1a5bf3d04f Provenance

Usage and purpose

According to [SWS_Dcm_91037], the element ControlDTCSettingModeSwitchInterface is a ModeSwitchInterface of the Diagnostic Communication Manager (DCM) provided as a provided port (PPortPrototype). Its primary task consists in notifying connected software components (SW-Cs) about the current state of the DTC setting mode (DTC Setting mode).

Here, Dcm_ControlDTCSettingModeSwitchInterface is used as the port interface [SWS_Dcm_91037]. Because the DCM declares this port as a provided port, the diagnostic module assumes the role of mode manager or sender. Application components can connect via corresponding required ports to receive status changes and adapt their internal behavior.

Interaction and System Integration

The interaction in the system network focuses on decoupling diagnostic commands from application logic:

  • Mode propagation: Via the provided port, the DCM informs the SW-Cs whether the storage and updating of diagnostic trouble codes is active or disabled [SWS_Dcm_91037]. The notification of the SW-Cs is likely to occur in the AUTOSAR runtime environment via standard mode-switch events of the RTE.
  • Diagnostic origin: Switching the DTC setting mode is presumably in direct context with UDS diagnostic services such as ControlDTCSetting (Service 0x85), via which an external tester can temporarily disable error logging.

Error Handling and Boundary Conditions

Since the specification in [SWS_Dcm_91037] defines neither specific error codes nor DET messages or return values, mode transmission occurs purely declaratively via the mechanisms of the RTE. No special call contexts or reentrancy requirements are indicated for the port declaration itself.

Usage and Interaction

Notification occurs via the port of the DCM to connected components [SWS_Dcm_91039]. Parameters, return values, or specific synchronous function calls are not defined in the port description [SWS_Dcm_91039]; transmission is therefore likely to correspond to the asynchronous broadcast semantics of a mode manager (interpretation).

type DcmModeRapidPowerShutDown [SWS_Dcm_91023] 📄 PDF

ModeDeclarationGroup representing the enable/disable state of rapid power shutdown

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: d451f77bd84c Provenance

The ModeDeclarationGroup DcmModeRapidPowerShutDown serves to represent the activation state for rapid power shutdown (Rapid Power Shutdown) in the ECU [SWS_Dcm_91023]. The element is assigned to category EXPLICIT_ORDER and defines two concrete modes: the initial mode DCM_ENABLE_RAPIDPOWERSHUTDOWN with the numerical value 0 and DCM_DISABLE_RAPIDPOWERSHUTDOWN with the value 1 [SWS_Dcm_91023]. For mode transitions, the transition value 255 (On transition value) is specified [SWS_Dcm_91023].

Interaction and Mode Management

In the overall system, the module DCM acts as mode manager for a series of diagnostic modes, which also includes DcmModeRapidPowerShutDown in the context of the diagnostic service 0x11 (ECU Reset) [SWS_Dcm_00775]. Within the basic software, the DCM defines the ModeDeclarationGroupPrototype DcmModeRapidPowerShutDown as provided-ModeGroup in its BSW module instance for this purpose based on this ModeDeclarationGroup [SWS_Dcm_00807].

Application software components (SW-Cs) that need to be informed about the current activation state of the rapid power shutdown connect the standardized service interface Dcm_ModeRapidPowerShutDownModeSwitchInterface [SWS_Dcm_91024]. Via its mode group modeRapidPowerShutDown, they receive corresponding mode switches of the DCM at runtime [SWS_Dcm_91024].

type DcmSecurityAccess [SWS_Dcm_91031] 📄 PDF

ModeDeclarationGroup representing the different diagnostic security levels Further modes to be added: {ecuc(Dcm/DcmConfigSet/DcmDsp/DcmDsp Security/DcmDspSecurityRow.SHORT-NAME)}

AI-GENERATED unreviewed Model: gemini-3.8-flash-medium · Effort: medium · Temperature: nicht steuerbar · Prompt: 776ea5647fe7 Provenance

The ModeDeclarationGroup DcmSecurityAccess of category EXPLICIT_ORDER represents the various diagnostic security levels of an ECU for the UDS service 0x27 (SecurityAccess) [SWS_Dcm_91031], [SWS_Dcm_00775]. As the initial mode, DCM_SEC_LEV_LOCKED with the fixed value 0 is specified by default [SWS_Dcm_91031], [SWS_Dcm_01327]. Additional security levels from DCM_SEC_LEV_1 to DCM_SEC_LEV_63 are added in a project- and application-specific manner via the configuration of the security rows under DcmDspSecurityRow [SWS_Dcm_91031], [SWS_Dcm_01327].

The DCM module assumes the central role as mode manager for this diagnostic mode [SWS_Dcm_00775]. With every change of the security level, the DCM updates the mode group DcmSecurityAccess with the newly assumed security status [SWS_Dcm_01329]. During an ongoing state transition between individual modes, the system signals the defined transition value 255 (On transition value) [SWS_Dcm_91031].

The propagation of the current security status to software components takes place via the service interface Dcm_SecurityAccessModeSwitchInterface [SWS_Dcm_91032]:

  • The DCM provides the ModeDeclarationGroupPrototype DcmSecurityAccess as a provided mode group (provided-ModeGroup) via the interface for this purpose [SWS_Dcm_01327], [SWS_Dcm_91032].
  • Each software component (SW-C) that needs to be informed about the current security level declares a dependency on the ModeSwitch interface Dcm_SecurityAccessModeSwitchInterface and integrates it as a required port [SWS_Dcm_91032].
  • The availability of the individual modes in the interface is subject to the same configuration variants as the underlying security rows [SWS_Dcm_91032].

Callbacks

Dcm_CopyRxData function

This function is called to provide the received data of an I-PDU segment (N-PDU) to the upper layer. Each call to this function provides the next part of the I-PDU data. The size of the remaining buffer is written to the position indicated by bufferSizePtr. This function might be called in interrupt context.

BufReq_ReturnType Dcm_CopyRxData (PduIdType id, const PduInfoType* info, PduLengthType* bufferSizePtr);
Dcm_CopyTxData function

This function is called to acquire the transmit data of an I-PDU segment (N-PDU). Each call to this function provides the next part of the I-PDU data unless retry->TpDataState is TP_ DATARETRY. In this case the function restarts to copy the data beginning at the offset from the current position indicated by retry->TxTpDataCnt. The size of the remaining data is written to the position indicated by availableDataPtr. This function might be called in interrupt context.

BufReq_ReturnType Dcm_CopyTxData (PduIdType id, const PduInfoType* info, const RetryInfoType* retry, PduLengthType* availableDataPtr);
Dcm_StartOfReception function

This function is called at the start of receiving an N-SDU. The N-SDU might be fragmented into multiple N-PDUs (FF with one or more following CFs) or might consist of a single N-PDU (SF). The service shall provide the currently available maximum buffer size when invoked with TpSdu Length equal to 0. This function might be called in interrupt context.

BufReq_ReturnType Dcm_StartOfReception (PduIdType id, const PduInfoType* info, PduLengthType TpSduLength, PduLengthType* bufferSizePtr);
Dcm_TpRxIndication function

Called after an I-PDU has been received via the TP API, the result indicates whether the transmission was successful or not. This function might be called in interrupt context.

void Dcm_TpRxIndication (PduIdType id, Std_ReturnType result);
Dcm_TpTxConfirmation function

This function is called after the I-PDU has been transmitted on its network, the result indicates whether the transmission was successful or not. This function might be called in interrupt context.

void Dcm_TpTxConfirmation (PduIdType id, Std_ReturnType result);
Dcm_TxConfirmation function

The lower layer communication interface module confirms the transmission of a PDU, or the failure to transmit a PDU. This function might be called in interrupt context.

void Dcm_TxConfirmation (PduIdType TxPduId, Std_ReturnType result);
